item.title: Elvis Presley and Eminem Rights Holders Sue Suno Over AI Music Clones
item.description:
Elvis Presley and Eminem Rights Holders Sue Suno Over AI Music Clones

AI music company Suno is facing two new lawsuits from rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music and the publisher of some of Eminem’s biggest records. The lawsuits claim that Suno illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic the two artists.

⚖️ Claims and Legal Arguments

The lawsuits allege that Suno creates imitations of artists using their identities and work without permission. Lawyers representing Presley’s rights holders argue that Suno violated Tennessee’s Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer’s voice.

In the Presley complaint, lawyers argue:

  • “Suno has mechanically encoded itself with artists’ identities, hard-work, creativity, and time, and harnessed them all for a consistent conveyor belt of cold hard cash.”
  • “Suno’s ravenous race to the bottom aims to make human creativity obsolete, coldly replicating without a license in seconds what takes years to learn, struggle with, maintain, and endlessly attempt to make better and perfect.”

These filings mirror a suit brought in September by Jason Isbell and others, which similarly alleged Suno created imitations of plaintiffs without directly asserting copyright infringement. Suno currently faces additional legal action from Sony, UMG, Isbell, Reservoir Media, and others.

🛡️ Suno’s Guardrails and Response

In response to the litigation, Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack told The Verge that “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work.”

To prevent misuse, Suno maintains the following platform safeguards:

  • Prompts requesting specific artists’ names and songs are prohibited.
  • Third-party providers screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse.
  • The company is working to strengthen existing guardrails and add new safeguards to protect artists and users.

#Suno #GenerativeAI #MusicIndustry #AILawsuits #Copyright

Source: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno

item.title: Preregistered Evaluation of Language Models on Numeric Values in Norwegian Law
item.description:
Preregistered Evaluation of Language Models on Numeric Values in Norwegian Law

A preregistered study evaluated language models on extracting numeric values from Norwegian statutes, regulations, and parliamentary decisions.

🔍 Overview

  • 916 items were extracted mechanically from Lovdata’s open data, each carrying the dated history of its provision.
  • The task asked language models for numeric values (NOK amounts, percentages, multiples of the National Insurance basic amount (G), and age limits) at a stated date.
  • Each answer can be classified as correct, outdated, wrong, or uninterpretable.

⚙️ Study Design

  • Two preregistered runs were performed on the same items.
  • First run: involved five models (names listed publicly only after local analysis). Hypothesis H1 (outdated answers more frequent for values after a model’s cutoff) could not be tested in substance; H2 and H3 were inconclusive.
  • Second run: preregistered and published before any calls, analysing eight models.

📊 Results

  • The pooled primary test of H1 in the second run supported the hypothesis (d = 17.8 percentage points, 95 % CI [7.7, 28.9], p = 0.0001).
  • In preregistered sensitivity analysis S8 (outdated counted only for the most recent differing value), d = 3.9 [-3.6, 12.7] (p = 0.1754), an interval that contains 0, so support for H1 is not robust.
  • H1 was supported in every other preregistered sensitivity analysis, but S8 is the only one giving both groups a single target value.
  • Share of outdated answers equal to the most recent value (H2) was 56.1 % [46.6, 65.0], an interval that contains 0.5.
  • The pooled test of a lower share correct in Nynorsk than in Bokmål (H3) was inconclusive.

Model Performance (Correct on Primary Items)

Model Correct %
Opus 5.5 46.7 %
Sonnet 4.6 40.2 %
  • Several models, among them Haiku 4.5, gave mostly uninterpretable answers.

📁 Data Availability

  • Items and keys are withheld.
  • Item IDs, per‑answer classes, code, and results are available on Zenodo.

#AIEvaluation #LanguageModels #NorwegianLaw #Preregistration

Source: norregel: a preregistered benchmark of dated numeric values in Norwegian law
